PhD Researcher at Oregon State University, Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and
Conservation Sciences.

Researching freshwater ecosystems, biological invasions, predator–prey interactions,
and fish–crayfish ecology using field surveys, controlled experiments, behavioral
observations, and quantitative ecological methods.

::: {.keywords}
Aquatic Ecology · Fisheries Science · Invasive Species · Freshwater Ecology ·
Crayfish Ecology · Smallmouth Bass · Predator–Prey Interactions ·
Behavioral Ecology · R
:::

## What I work on

My dissertation examines how non-native Smallmouth Bass (*Micropterus dolomieu*),
invasive Ringed Crayfish (*Faxonius neglectus*), and native Signal Crayfish
(*Pacifastacus leniusculus*) interact in the Willamette and Umpqua River systems,
and whether one invader can slow another. The work combines field diet analysis,
stable isotopes, mesocosm experiments, and spatial stream network modeling.

[Read more about the research →](research.qmd)

## Currently

- Completing three dissertation chapters; expected graduation March 2027.
- Running temperature-controlled predation trials in a three-compartment mesocosm system.
- Building reproducible analysis pipelines in R and Quarto.
